summary_en: This Phase 1 study tests CRD3874-SI, a STING agonist, in people with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including sarcoma and Merkel cell carcinoma. CRD3874-SI is given as a weekly IV infusion in 28-day cycles, starting at 0.1 mg/kg, with four weekly doses in cycles 1 and 2 and three weekly doses from cycle 3 on. The study measures safety and side effects to find the highest dose with few or mild side effects; it is a Phase 1 study.
summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 prueba CRD3874-SI, un agonista de STING, en personas con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos, incluidos sarcoma y carcinoma de células de Merkel. CRD3874-SI se administra como infusión intravenosa semanal en ciclos de 28 días, comenzando con 0.1 mg/kg, con cuatro dosis semanales en los ciclos 1 y 2 y tres dosis semanales desde el ciclo 3. El estudio mide la seguridad y los efectos secundarios para encontrar la dosis más alta con pocos efectos secundarios o leves; es un estudio de Fase 1.
who_for: Age 18 or older and able to give written informed consent.
Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor that progressed on at least one systemic therapy, or has no standard treatment, or the person is intolerant or declin
Cancer type and prior treatment lines must fit a listed group, such as head and neck squamous cell, adenoid cystic, Merkel cell, sarcoma, melanoma, or non-small
Measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and adequate blood, liver, kidney, and heart function.
not_for: Known prior severe hypersensitivity to the study drug or its components, including polyethylene glycol.
Clinically significant immunosuppression, or systemic immunosuppressive therapy or steroid doses above the stated limits.
Prior organ transplant or allogeneic stem-cell transplant; autologous transplant considered only if at least 5 years ago.
Symptomatic or systemically treated autoimmune disease within 2 years, or uncontrolled medical conditions, active infection needing systemic therapy, or symptom
Resting QTc of 470 ms or more, or currently receiving study therapy in another investigational study.
